comparator.name: Bachelor Milieu-natuurwetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: The current 180-EC bachelor comprises a 60-EC compulsory propedeuse, 65 EC selected from a 70-EC restricted-choice list, 30 EC of free elective space and a 25-EC graduation phase. To represent the generic programme neutrally, the restricted-choice component follows official study-guide order and includes thirteen of the fourteen 5-EC modules, omitting only AI en maatschappij; no UCR-fit consideration was used in that choice.

core: Environmental natural sciences linking Earth, water, soils, ecosystems and human activity
Environmental problem analysis using mathematics, data, experiments and research methods
Climate, energy, circular-resource and sustainability transitions
adjacent: Biodiversity, pollution, ecosystem resilience and food-environment relations
Environmental policy, decision-making and science-practice connections
Renewable energy, circular systems and environmental economics
Environmental data, GIS, modelling, hypotheses and scientific communication
questions: How do coupled Earth and ecological systems respond to human pressures?
How can evidence be used to analyse and solve environmental problems?
Which technological, economic and governance choices enable sustainable transitions?

alternatives.label: Environmental systems, evidence & sustainable solutions
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum integrates Earth and ecosystem science, climate, soils, water, quantitative evidence, pollution, circular resources, energy and governance.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Milieu-natuurwetenschappen: an integrated environmental natural-science programme linking Earth and ecosystem processes, climate, pollution, soils and water with data, observation, circular-resource solutions and sustainability governance.
progression: Environmental science, programming and mathematical foundations precede climate, observation, soils, water, numerical methods, biogeochemistry, remediation, research and advanced sustainability applications. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Climate, energy & circular systems
alternatives.labelReason: This curriculum centres climate mitigation and adaptation, renewable systems, circular resource use and the economic choices that shape environmental transitions.
alternatives.concept: A climate-and-resources direction combining climate science and communication with renewable-system design, life-cycle analysis, circular recovery, environmental observation and economic analysis of transition choices.
progression: Earth science, sustainability, economics, research and mathematics foundations precede climate communication, life-cycle analysis, observation, renewable design, public economics, recovery, research, econometrics and advanced behavioural analysis. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; nine 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes decarbonisation, renewable-system design, circular resource use and transition economics the organising priority. It differs from the closest programme by ten courses and 75 EC in each direction.

alternatives.label: Environmental policy, governance & participation
alternatives.labelReason: This curriculum combines environmental systems and spatial evidence with sociology, economics, politics, participation, communication and sustainability governance.
alternatives.concept: A policy-and-governance direction examining how institutions, economic choices, public participation, environmental justice and communication shape sustainable environmental decisions.
progression: Environmental and social-science foundations precede qualitative and quantitative research, policy, economics, spatial evidence, water governance, public participation, communication and advanced sustainability institutions. Formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: This route makes institutions, public participation, environmental justice and communication the organising priority. It differs from the closest programme by thirteen courses and 97.5 EC in each direction, and from the climate-and-resources route by twelve courses and 90 EC in each direction.

blocks: Both introduce environmental systems and the relationship between human activity and planetary limits.
Both connect natural-science knowledge to sustainability problems and responses; OU covers the field in a dedicated environmental-science module.
Both provide introductory programming and computational problem-solving foundations.
Both provide mathematical methods for natural and environmental sciences.
Both develop research design and quantitative evidence skills; OU applies them specifically to environmental science.
Both examine social influence and behaviour relevant to climate choices; OU applies psychology directly to climate action.
UCR embeds chemistry in environmental gateway and advanced courses but lacks a selected dedicated chemistry module of equal scope.
UCR does not include a selected dedicated physiology module in these alternatives.
UCR embeds physical-science concepts in sustainability study but lacks a selected dedicated physics module of equal scope.
Both examine Earth processes, resources, pollution and human-environment relations.
Both use systems models and evidence to analyse coupled environmental change.
Both establish evolutionary and biodiversity foundations.
Both examine ecosystem functioning and its relationship to human well-being.
Both analyse linked soil, groundwater and catchment processes.
Both include integrated application of natural-science evidence; UCR applies laboratory and modelling work to biogeochemical systems.
UCR addresses contaminants and remediation but lacks a selected dedicated environmental-toxicology module.
UCR addresses climate, resources and sustainability but lacks a selected dedicated food-health-environment module.
Both integrate climate science, impacts, adaptation and mitigation.
Both examine renewable-energy systems and sustainable system design.
Both consider spatial, nature-based responses to climate and sustainability challenges.
Both develop data analysis and inference for research questions.
Both apply advanced data methods to complex or dynamic systems.
Both use geographic information systems to analyse environmental change.
The OU thesis is a required 15-EC environmental-science graduation project; UCR optional independent research is shown in parallel as a comparison-only opportunity.
Both analyse environmental policy, governance actors and collective decision-making.
Both apply economic reasoning to public and environmental choices.
Both examine citizen initiatives, collective action and participation in sustainability change.
OU retains 30 EC of free elective space; UCR flexibility is expressed through the complete selected 180-EC programmes rather than a separate unassigned block.

notes.text: Open Universiteit provides a prescribed environmental natural-sciences sequence in mathematics, chemistry, physics, physiology, laboratory science, environmental toxicology, food and environmental research, followed by a formal 15-EC thesis. UCR can combine substantial Earth science, ecology, climate, data, resources, governance and sustainability study, but does not reproduce that full specialist natural-science sequence.

selection.assessment: The closest programme integrates environmental systems, quantitative evidence, climate, pollution and sustainable solutions. Climate/energy/circular systems and environmental policy/governance form two further evidenced, coherent and mechanically feasible directions. They differ pairwise by at least 75 EC, so production stops at the three-alternative maximum.
